title: Endpoint quantile profiles & benchmark harness integration
creator: Priya Patel
description: Add fine-grained p95/p99 latency collection and visualizations tied to route/model/region and wire this into the existing load/benchmark harness. Goals: (1) Emit and store per-request quantile-aware latency profiles alongside tokens/sec and sequence-length metadata; (2) Provide minute/hour rollups and long-term rollups for trend/regression detection; (3) Expose dashboards that let SRE/ENG slice by route, model, model_variant, region, and rollout stage; (4) Integrate automated regression checks into nightly/PR harness runs so a spike in tail latency or tokens/sec degradation triggers an alert and a failed regression job.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark harness emits per-request telemetry that includes: route, model, model_variant, region, request_id, sequence_length, tokens_generated, latency_ms
Per-minute and per-hour quantile rollups (p50/p90/p95/p99) are stored in the TSDB and queryable by route/model/region
A Grafana dashboard exists with: heatmap of p95/p99 by model_version and region, percentile trend line, tokens/sec overlay, and a baseline comparison panel
Nightly regression job computes change from baseline and fails when relative p95 increase > 10% AND absolute increase > 25ms for top-tier routes
End-to-end test: synthetic workload across small/medium/large sequence lengths validates telemetry correctness and dashboard panels show expected deltas
decisions: Use t-digest based quantile sketches at ingestion to keep memory and merge costs bounded versus storing raw histograms
Emit both raw latency_ms and t-digest sketches from the harness so we can recompute quantiles if needed for re-rollups
Store minute-level rollups in ClickHouse and hourly/day rollups as stitched aggregates for longer retention; Prometheus not used for high-cardinality quantiles
Cardinality will be limited by capping model_variant tags to 'variant-stable'|'variant-canary'|'variant-alpha' when pipeline sees >50 variants in 24h
Regression thresholds are configurable per-route via the console; default is relative 10% p95 increase with 25ms absolute floor
implementation_plan: Instrument benchmark harness to add telemetry payload for each request (PR: runtime/bench/telemetry instrumentation)
Add t-digest serialization + sampling helper in runtime telemetry lib (language bindings: Go and Python)
Ingest sketches into processing pipeline (collector) and perform minute-level merges
Write ClickHouse schema migration + ingestion consumer to store rollups and tokens/sec metrics
Create Grafana dashboards and reusable panels (heatmap + quantile trends + tokens/sec overlay)
Add nightly CI job: run multi-model workload, push telemetry, evaluate quantile changes against baseline, post results to Slack and mark regression status in PRs
Add alerting rules and console UI knobs to tune thresholds per-route
